QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_2

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund has 40 investors holding units with aggregate committed value of INR 800 crore. At a meeting called under Regulation 29, investors representing INR 612 crore vote in favour of winding up. Does the resolution pass?

answer.text: Yes — INR 612 cr / INR 800 cr = 76.5%, above the 75% threshold
No — headcount of voters is not disclosed; headcount majority is also required
No — winding-up resolutions need unanimous 100% consent
Yes, but only if SEBI concurrently directs winding up

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 29(1)(c) requires 75% of investors BY VALUE of their investment to pass the winding-up resolution. 612 / 800 = 76.5%, which clears the 75% threshold. Headcount is NOT a secondary requirement — the AIF Regulations are purely value-weighted. SEBI direction (Reg 29(1)(d)) is a SEPARATE independent trigger, not a conjunction. The Trap: Unanimity (option C) is wrong — AIFs never need 100% for winding up. Dual headcount + value (option B) borrows from mutual-fund unit-holder rules. SEBI concurrence (option D) confuses the independent Reg 29(1)(d) trigger with a joint requirement. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 75%-by-value threshold for winding up across categories. XIX-D applies it to Cat I/II. The 75% value threshold also shows up for waiving the mandatory exit option on material PPM change. Manager's Pro-Tip: On voluntary winding-up, run the value-threshold calculation off the latest NAV register, not committed capital, for Cat III open-ended schemes where capital accounts fluctuate with NAV moves. The 75% test is on INVESTED value at the date of the resolution.
